themes_detail.label: Graffiti explosion in Elmhurst
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints skyrocketed to 30 this week—a 1400% spike versus the 2.0 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—signaling either a coordinated tagging campaign or deteriorating enforcement in CD 404.
evidence: 30 graffiti complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 16.88)
1400% increase from baseline—highest statistical anomaly in dataset
Concentrated acute spike suggests new pattern, not seasonal trend
reporting_angles: Ground reporting: map the affected blocks and photograph the tags to determine if organized crew or dispersed vandalism
City response: when did Parks/Sanitation last respond to graffiti removal requests in this district, and are crews understaffed?

themes_detail.label: Street infrastructure damage surge
themes_detail.summary: Damaged street signs (9 complaints this week vs. 2.1 weekly average) and degraded curb conditions (5 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.8 average) indicate accelerating street-level deterioration, with a combined z-score of 7.42 and 9.81 respectively.
evidence: Street Sign - Damaged: 9 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.1 weekly average (z-score: 7.42, 324% increase)
Curb Condition: 5 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.8 weekly average (z-score: 9.81, 567% increase)
280 street condition complaints over 90 days—consistent chronic issue now accelerating in severity
reporting_angles: Investigate: are DOT inspections occurring at normal frequency in CD 404, or is maintenance backlogged?
City budget angle: does the district's repeated capital budget request for street/park reconstruction signal a known resource gap?

themes_detail.label: Building inspection activity spike
themes_detail.summary: Special Projects Inspection Team (SPIT) complaints surged to 3 this week—a 2300% increase versus the 0.1 weekly baseline—suggesting either intensive enforcement action or systemic building/code compliance failures in the district.
evidence: SPIT complaints: 3 THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average (z-score: 8.69, 2300% spike)
274 DOB building permits filed in last 90 days (196 alterations, 28 new buildings, 6 demolitions) suggest active development pressure
Residential Disposal Complaint also up 344% (5 vs. 1.1 avg)—possible indicator of construction-related debris or occupied-unit violations
reporting_angles: FOIA request: what triggered SPIT deployments this week—are city inspectors investigating specific buildings or properties?
Developer pressure: how do the four active ULURP rezonings (50-20 108th St, 47-03 108th St, Walk to Park site) correlate with inspection intensity?

themes_detail.label: Hazmat and elevator safety concerns
themes_detail.summary: Hazardous materials complaints jumped to 3 last week (1100% above the 0.2 weekly average), and elevator complaints reached 26 two weeks ago (252% increase vs. 7.4 average)—both high-severity safety signals affecting residential occupancy and building code compliance.
evidence: Hazardous Materials: 3 complaints last week vs. 0.2 weekly average (z-score: 6.35, 1100% increase)
Elevator: 26 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 7.4 weekly average (z-score: 6.13, 252% increase)
Two distinct safety categories spiking simultaneously suggest either new construction-phase disruption or deferred maintenance across multiple buildings
reporting_angles: Safety audit: contact building owners and DOB to identify which properties have active elevator or hazmat violations
Resident impact: interview tenants in affected buildings to document safety risks and response times from landlords/city

themes_detail.label: Food vendor enforcement escalation
themes_detail.summary: Mobile food vendor complaints jumped to 4 last week—a 700% spike versus the 0.5 weekly baseline—suggesting either a coordinated city enforcement sweep or an influx of unlicensed vendors in the district.
evidence: Mobile Food Vendor: 4 complaints last week vs. 0.5 weekly average (z-score: 7.0, 700% increase)
Isolated spike—only 4 complaints total, but represents dramatic departure from baseline
reporting_angles: Check with Department of Health: was there a targeted enforcement action or vendor licensing crackdown in Elmhurst/Corona last week?
Street economy angle: interview food vendors about licensing barriers and enforcement patterns in this predominantly immigrant, working-class district
